items.title: Restraint of the Faculties Reopens: Six Steps to Guarding the Senses

items.zh: 云何根律儀？謂如有一，能善安住密護根門，防守正念，常委正念，乃至廣說。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first yogic process, the third chapter, the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation, part two. …What is restraint of the faculties? It is like one who is able to skilfully abide in closely guarding the sense-gates, maintaining mindfulness, sustaining mindfulness — and so on, to be explained at length.

items.title: Closely Guarding the Sense-Gates, and Obtaining the Mindfulness That Guards Them

items.zh: 云何名為密護根門？謂防守正念，常委正念，廣說乃至防護意根，及正修行意根律儀。如是名為密護根門。云何名為防守正念？謂如有一，密護根門增上力故，攝受多聞、思惟、修習。由聞思修增上力故，獲得正念。
items.en: What is called closely guarding the sense-gates? It is maintaining mindfulness, sustaining mindfulness — and so on at length, down to protecting the mind-faculty and correctly practising restraint of the mind-faculty. This is called closely guarding the sense-gates. What is called maintaining mindfulness? It is that one, through the power of closely guarding the sense-gates, takes up extensive learning, reflection, and cultivation. Through the power of learning, reflection, and cultivation, one obtains mindfulness.

items.title: The Four-Part Discipline Behind Mindfulness, and Sustaining It Without Interruption

items.zh: 為欲令此所得正念無忘失故，能趣證故，不失壞故。於時時中，即於多聞、若思、若修，正作瑜伽，正勤修習，不息加行、不離加行。如是由此多聞思修所集成念，於時時中，善能防守正聞思修瑜伽作用。如是名為防守正念。云何名為常委正念？謂於此念恒常所作、委細所作。當知此中，恒常所作，名無間作；委細所作，名殷重作。即於如是無間所作、殷重所作，總說名為常委正念。
items.en: In order that this mindfulness once obtained not be forgotten, that it lead to genuine realisation, and that it not be lost or destroyed — from time to time, with regard to learning, reflection, and cultivation, one correctly engages in yogic practice, correctly and diligently cultivates it, never resting from the effort and never abandoning it. Thus, through the mindfulness accumulated by such learning, reflection, and cultivation, one is, from time to time, well able to guard the function of correct hearing, reflection, and cultivation. This is called maintaining mindfulness. …What is called sustaining mindfulness? It is that this mindfulness is exercised constantly, and exercised thoroughly. It should be understood that exercising it constantly is called uninterrupted practice, and exercising it thoroughly is called earnest practice. This uninterrupted and earnest practice together are called, in sum, sustaining mindfulness.

items.zh: 如其所有防守正念，如是於念能不忘失；如其所有常委正念，如是即於無忘失念得任持力。即由如是功能勢力，制伏色聲香味觸法。云何名為念防護意？
items.en: Insofar as one maintains mindfulness, one does not lose mindfulness; insofar as one sustains mindfulness, one gains the power to uphold that unforgotten mindfulness. Through the force of this capacity, one masters forms, sounds, scents, tastes, tactile objects, and mental objects. What is called protecting the mind with mindfulness?

items.title: Protecting the Mind Itself: A Precise Map of How a Single Glance Becomes Craving

items.zh: 謂眼色為緣生眼識，眼識無間生分別意識，由此分別意識，於可愛色色將生染著，於不可愛色色將生憎恚。即由如是念增上力，能防護此非理分別起煩惱意，令其不生所有煩惱。如是耳鼻舌身廣說，當知亦爾。意法為緣生意識，即此意識有與非理分別俱行，能起煩惱；由此意識，於可愛色法將生染著，於不可愛色法將生憎恚。亦由如是念增上力，能防護此非理分別起煩惱意，令其不生所有煩惱。如是名為念防護意。
items.en: It is that the eye and form, as condition, give rise to eye-consciousness; immediately following eye-consciousness, discriminating mental-consciousness arises. Through this discriminating mental-consciousness, one is about to become attached to an agreeable form [of the form seen, as the mind discriminates it], or about to feel hatred towards a disagreeable one. It is precisely through the power of mindfulness that one is able to guard against this afflictive mind arising from unwise discrimination, preventing any affliction from arising. So too, at length, should it be understood regarding the ear, nose, tongue, and body. …Mind and mental object, as condition, give rise to mental-consciousness; this very mental-consciousness, conjoined with unwise discrimination, is able to give rise to affliction. Through this mental-consciousness, one is about to become attached to an agreeable form [recalled or imagined as a mental object], or about to feel hatred towards a disagreeable one. It is likewise through the power of mindfulness that one is able to guard against this afflictive mind arising from unwise discrimination, preventing any affliction from arising. This is called protecting the mind.

items.title: Resting in Equanimity: Two Ways to Release What Has Already Stirred

items.zh: 云何名為行平等位？平等位者，謂或善捨、或無記捨。由彼於此非理分別起煩惱意善防護已，正行善捨、無記捨中，由是說名行平等位。
items.en: What is called resting in equanimity? Equanimity means either wholesome relinquishment or neutral relinquishment. Once one has skilfully guarded against this afflictive mind arising from unwise discrimination, and correctly rests within wholesome relinquishment or neutral relinquishment, this is called resting in equanimity.

items.zh: 如是名為行平等位。云何於此非理分別起煩惱意能善防護？
items.en: This is called resting in equanimity. How does one skilfully guard, here, against the afflicted mind that arises from unwise discrimination?

items.title: Two Aspects Unpacked in Full: What "Not Grasping the Mark" Actually Means, Moment by Moment

items.zh: 謂於色聲香味觸法，不取其相，不取隨好，終不依彼發生諸惡不善尋思，令心流漏。若彼有時忘失念故，或由煩惱極熾盛故，雖離取相及取隨好，而復發生惡不善法，令心流漏，便修律儀。由是二相，故能於此非理分別起煩惱意能善防護。云何此意由是二相善防護已，正行善捨或無記捨？謂即由是二種相故。云何二相？謂如所說防護眼根，及正修行眼根律儀。如說眼根防護律儀，防護耳鼻舌身意根，及正修行意根律儀，當知亦爾。由是二相，於其善捨、無記捨中，令意正行。云何於眼所識色中不取其相？言取相者，謂於眼識所行色中，由眼識故取所行相，是名於眼所識色中執取其相。若能遠離如是眼識所行境相，是名於眼所識色中不取其相。如於其眼所識色中，如是於耳鼻舌身意所識法中，當知亦爾。云何於眼所識色中不取隨好？取隨好者，謂即於眼所識色中，眼識無間俱生分別意識，執取所行境相，或能起貪、或能起瞋、或能起癡，是名於眼所識色中執取隨好。若能遠離此所行相，於此所緣不生意識，是名於眼所識色中不取隨好。
items.en: Regarding forms, sounds, scents, tastes, tactile objects, and mental objects: not grasping their general mark, not grasping their alluring details — never, on that basis, giving rise to unwholesome, improper trains of thought that let the mind leak out into affliction. …It is through these two aspects that one is able to skilfully guard against this afflictive mind arising from unwise discrimination. …What is not grasping the general mark in a form known by the eye? Grasping the mark means that, within the form that is eye-consciousness's own domain, one grasps, by means of eye-consciousness, the mark of that domain — this is called grasping the mark within a form known by the eye. …If one is able to be free of this domain-object as eye-consciousness presents it, this is called not grasping the mark within a form known by the eye. …What is not grasping the alluring details in a form known by the eye? Grasping the alluring details means that, within a form known by the eye, the discriminating mental-consciousness that arises immediately following eye-consciousness grasps at that domain-object, and is thereby able to give rise to craving, or to hatred, or to delusion — this is called grasping the alluring details within a form known by the eye. If one is able to be free of this domain-object, such that no [afflicted] mental-consciousness arises with regard to it, this is called not grasping the alluring details within a form known by the eye.

items.zh: 如於其眼所識色中，如是於耳鼻舌身意所識法中，當知亦爾。
items.en: As it is with forms known by the eye, so too it should be understood with the objects known by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

blocks.text: Fascicle 23 explains two of the provisions in detail: **restraint of the senses** and **moderation in eating**. Today's passage is one of the clearest accounts in Buddhist literature of how perception turns into craving, moment by moment.

One "closely guards the sense-gates, maintains mindfulness, sustains mindfulness", protects the mind, rests in equanimity, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng: a gate is where things go out and come in; through the six senses false discriminations go out and the "dust" of objects comes in.

Mindfulness is obtained "through the power of learning, reflection, and cultivation". Then it must be kept from being lost, through constant and earnest practice. Venerable Miào Jìng: without mindfulness, however much Dharma one studies is as good as unlearned, because it never comes to mind.

"The eye and form, as condition, give rise to eye-consciousness; immediately following eye-consciousness, discriminating mental consciousness arises." Eye-consciousness simply sees. The mental consciousness that follows discriminates the object as lovely or unlovely, and from that, craving or aversion arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: mindfulness is the gatekeeper that does not let greed, hatred, and delusion in.

If something has already stirred, one rests in equanimity, wholesome or neutral, and does not follow it. Master Cháng Bǎi: Theravāda teachers often teach this: "pay it no heed and do not follow it." Venerable Miào Jìng: greed and hatred are not even; equanimity is what is even.

"Grasping the mark" means that eye-consciousness grasps its object. Master Cháng Bǎi: at that point there is only grasping; greed and hatred have not yet arisen. The trouble comes with the **alluring details**, which mental consciousness adds. Venerable Miào Jìng: when the mind lets out afflictions, it "leaks", like a sore oozing pus.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how is mindfulness obtained?
options: through the power of learning, reflection, and cultivation
quiz.why: "Through the power of learning, reflection, and cultivation, one obtains mindfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the six faculties are the basis, learning, reflection, and cultivation the gathering cause; so mindfulness is gained, and with it the sense-gates are guarded.

quiz.q: Why does Venerable Miào Jìng say the faculties are called "gates"?
options: because the faculties are as solid as a house
a gate is where things go out and come in: false discrimination goes out through the faculties, and the dust of outer objects comes in
because a gate can be shut forever
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a gate is a place of going out and coming in; through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, false discriminations go out and the dust of outer objects comes in.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call the "constant" and the "thorough" exercise of mindfulness?
options: constant is intermittent practice; thorough is casual practice
constant is wholesome practice; thorough is neutral practice
constant is learning; thorough is reflection
constant exercise is uninterrupted practice; thorough exercise is earnest practice
quiz.why: "It should be understood that exercising it constantly is called uninterrupted practice, and exercising it thoroughly is called earnest practice." Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping it working in the mind without a break, hearing, reflecting, and cultivating without slackness, is uninterrupted practice.

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, what happens to one's study of the Dharma without mindfulness?
options: however much one learns, it is as if one had learned nothing, since it does not come to mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: without mindfulness, however much Dharma one studies is as good as unlearned, because it never comes to mind. That is why the text says to maintain mindfulness so it is not forgotten.

quiz.q: In the treatise's account of seeing, what arises immediately after eye-consciousness?
quiz.why: "The eye and form, as condition, give rise to eye-consciousness; immediately following eye-consciousness, discriminating mental-consciousness arises." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first moment, the sudden mind, belongs to eye-consciousness; the second and third, the seeking and deciding minds, belong to the sixth consciousness.

quiz.q: What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for protecting the mind with mindfulness?
options: mindfulness is a gatekeeper who keeps greed, hatred, and delusion out
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: mindfulness is like a gatekeeper that protects the mind, not letting greed, hatred, and delusion in; this is protecting the mind with mindfulness.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which consciousness grasps the alluring details, and what does it give rise to?
options: eye-consciousness, giving rise to wholesome mind
the discriminating mind-consciousness arising right after eye-consciousness grasps the object and gives rise to craving, hatred, or delusion
the storehouse consciousness, giving rise to concentration
quiz.why: "The discriminating mental-consciousness that arises immediately following eye-consciousness grasps at that domain-object, and is thereby able to give rise to craving, or to hatred, or to delusion." Master Cháng Bǎi: not grasping the details means discriminating consciousness no longer goes on to produce greed, hatred, and delusion.
